  "sql": "SELECT p.category, count(DISTINCT r.id) AS refund_count FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON o.id = r.order_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY refund_count DESC LIMIT 1",
  "tables_used": ["refunds", "orders", "order_items", "products"],
  "rationale": "To find the product category with the highest number of refunds, we join refunds through orders to order_items and products. The key fix is using COUNT(DISTINCT r.id) instead of COUNT(*) to avoid counting the same refund multiple times when an order contains items from multiple categories. This ensures each refund is counted only once, attributed to each product category in that order. We group by category, sort by refund count descending, and limit to 1 to get the top category."
